_comment: Edit this file, not the code. Credentials never live here - they come from the SENEYE_USER / SENEYE_PWD environment variables.

site.title: Seagrass Nursery Monitoring
site.subtitle: Posidonia oceanica conditioning systems, North Mole, Gibraltar

systems._comment: The five nursery systems. Each Seneye sits in a sump, and a sump serves the tanks listed against it.

devices._comment: Seneye device id -> the sump it monitors, read from GET /v1/devices on 21 Sept 2026. The system letter, tank list and label are looked up from the sump. If a unit is moved, change its sump here; readings already stored keep the mapping they were collected under.

parameters._comment: band = the nursery's own working range (shaded on the charts). hard = the range outside which a reading is flagged critical; null means no critical threshold set. Temperature, pH and NH3 are TNP set points supplied by Lewis Stagnetto, 21 Sept 2026. They are operating set points for this nursery, not published tolerances for Posidonia oceanica.

nutrients._comment: In-situ samples taken by hand at the sumps, on different instruments from the Seneye probes. Read live from the Google Sheet on every run: paste the sheet's URL below, and in Sheets use File > Share > Publish to web > Nutrient > Comma-separated values so the harvester can read it without a login. Rows are matched to sumps by the Tank ID column (A12 -> SA12) and keyed on date + sump, so a corrected sheet overwrites the old values rather than duplicating them. If the fetch fails the stored samples are left untouched and data/nutrients.xlsx is used if present.
nutrients.method_note: In-situ spot samples: handheld meters and test kits, read by eye. Accuracy and resolution differ from the Seneye probes, so the two are shown as separate measurements and never averaged together.

insitu_reference._comment: Reference ranges for colouring the in-situ sample table. typical = ordinary local seawater (green). Between typical and outer is amber, meaning off typical but not alarming. Beyond outer is red. Derived from published seawater values for the western Mediterranean and Strait of Gibraltar and converted into the units this sheet uses; the workings and sources are in the README. These describe SEAWATER, not what Posidonia requires, and a red cell is a prompt to check the reading and the kit, not evidence of a problem. Phosphate, calcium and magnesium are read in ppm; in seawater 1 ppm is ~1.03 mg/L, so the same numbers serve for both and nothing is converted.

temp_c.basis: TNP nursery operating set points, not a seawater range

salinity_ppt.basis: Atlantic inflow ~36.2 to Mediterranean outflow ~38.4 at the Strait

ph.basis: surface ocean pH ~8.1; outer bounds are the nursery set points

no3.basis: western Mediterranean surface nitrate under ~4 umol/kg = 0.25 mg/L as NO3

no2.basis: upper-ocean nitrite 10-1000 nmol/L = up to ~0.046 mg/L as NO2

nh3.basis: surface ammonium typically under a few umol/L; check whether the kit reports total ammonia or free NH3

po4.basis: western Mediterranean surface phosphate ~0.16 umol/kg = 0.015 ppm as PO4

ca.basis: 412 ppm at S=35, scaling with salinity to ~452 ppm at S=38.4

mg.basis: 1290 ppm at S=35, scaling with salinity to ~1415 ppm at S=38.4

maintenance._comment: Issue tracking and planned jobs for anyone working at the nursery. Two tabs in the maintenance sheet: one row per fault, one row per recurring job. This log names people, so it is NOT published with the student dashboard: the board is written to board/ which the Pages workflow does not upload and .gitignore keeps out of the repo. Disabled for now: the maintenance log lives in Google until a private repo is available. Set enabled to true to start building the board, and publish to true only once you have decided that the log can be public, or set anonymise to true to strip names from the export.

issues._comment: gid is the number after gid= in the tab's URL. Publish this tab to the web as CSV the same way as the Nutrient tab.
